title: zoom_rung is stored on View though purely derivable from scale/fit, so every direct scale mutation must manually keep the pair coherent
detail: The comment itself says rung is a pure function of effective zoom, yet it is stored alongside scale as independent state. Two 'companion' patches in this same diff show the drift cost; any future site setting scale without the pairing silently renders the wrong ladder. zoom_rung_of(v.scale/camera_fit(v)) at read time needs no invariant.
recommended_fix: Either derive the rung at read time (zoom_rung_of(v.scale / camera_fit(v)) — camera_fit is a pure View read) or add one view_set_zoom(v, z) setter that pairs scale and rung; migrate camera_update, run.odin, and palcheck to it.

title: Assist route-glow path geometry still computes with uncapped band_world while the drawn ribbon now uses link_width_capped — paths diverge when a clamp engages
detail: Before this diff both call sites used the same uncapped formula, so glow path and drawn ribbon agreed. wire_paths_compute moved to the capped clearance but draw_glow_edge kept band_world, so for a clamped bundle with route flags on the glow polyline detours on a different clearance than the rendered wire — contradicting the PR's 'flags-on path obeys the covenant' claim at the geometry level (only the halo width, line 425, is capped).
recommended_fix: In draw_glow_edge replace band_world(...) with link_width_capped(v, topo, bundles, bi) for the bundle's own clearance basis, matching wire_paths_compute.

title: band_width is now dead — zero callers in the repo — with a stale doc claiming stroke/halo/rider consumers derive from it
detail: After the migration every consumer calls link_width_capped or band_world; band_width has no callers left. Its doc still claims the strokes/riders/halos derive from it — the comment now misdescribes the architecture, and the proc is silent dead weight.
recommended_fix: Delete band_width, or if kept as the endpoint-blind accessor, fix the doc to say consumers derive from link_width_world/band_world and that no caller remains.

title: On the app's no-sprite-sheet fallback path, zero bboxes make sprite_puck_target return 0, so link_width_capped clamps router-touching bundles to invisible width 0
detail: When sprites_load fails the app continues (only harness/palcheck abort), leaving bboxes unparsed: min(0/110, 1.30) = 0 puck target, so the covenant cap for any router endpoint is 0 and bundles clamp to width 0 — invisible links in the documented fallback mode. The deferred-work entry covers the fallback's rung tables but not this zero-cap consequence.
recommended_fix: Extend the existing primitive-fallback deferred item: guard node_draw_size_world (or link_width_capped) to skip the clamp when v.sprites.ok is false, matching the pre-LOOK fallback behavior.

title: draw_bundles keeps its flow parameter but discards it every iteration (_ = flow) — dead signature coupling after the lane-stripe removal
evidence:
app/render/view.odin:937:
draw_bundles :: proc(v: ^View, topo: ^pp.Topology, bundles: ^pp.Bundles, flow: ^pp.Flow_State, crisis: ^pp.Crisis_State, desat: f32, paths: []Wire_Path) {
app/render/view.odin:963:
		_ = flow // the lane caps died with the lane stripes (LOOK §3); riders read them per-pipe
app/render/view.odin:541:
	draw_bundles(v, topo, bundles, flow, crisis, desat_f, paths[:])
detail: Lane stripes were the only flow consumer in draw_bundles; the parameter now exists solely so the single call site (draw_world) need not change, and the discard sits inside the per-bundle loop rather than at function entry. Minor coupling debt that obscures what the draw actually reads.
recommended_fix: Drop flow from draw_bundles' signature and the draw_world call site (riders in draw_packets keep their own bundle_lane_caps_view reads), or at minimum hoist the discard out of the loop.
